1. YMCA OF MONTREAL FONDS (P0145) — OVERVIEW
   URL: https://concordia.accesstomemory.org/ymca-of-montreal-fonds-2
================================================================================

Reference Code: P0145
Creator: YMCA of Montreal (1851–)
Repository: Concordia University Records Management & Archives, Library's Special Collections and Archives, and Visual Collections Repository

HISTORICAL BACKGROUND:
- First YMCA founded in London, England in 1844 by George Williams, age 23
- Religious (Evangelical Protestant) movement for young men
- At the 1851 world's fair in London, YMCA pamphlets distributed to Montrealers
- Inaugural meeting of the Montreal YMCA at St. Helen Street Baptist Church, November 1851
- Montreal YMCA can claim to be the first in North America (Boston, New York, Toronto started about the same time)

SCOPE AND CONTENT:
- Documents the mission, structure, senior personnel, administration, programs, activities, facilities, and evolution of the Montreal YMCA (as of 2009, Le Y du Québec) from its founding in 1851 to the late 20th century
- Documents relationships with external bodies including other Canadian YMCAs, National Council of YMCAs of Canada, YMCA movement in North America and the world
- Educational programs grew to become Sir George Williams College/University (one of Concordia University's founding institutions)
- In the 1970s, shift in Quebec government policy meant increased emphasis on community recreational programs
- Community development programs including immigrant, crime prevention, and offender rehabilitation programs were added
- Includes materials amassed by Harold C. Cross and Murray C. Ross for their histories of the Montreal Association and the YMCA in Canada, respectively
- Also includes materials from the former Metropolitan Montreal YMCA library/documentation centre

MATERIALS INCLUDE:
- Correspondence of YMCA officials and others
- Board and committee minutes and related records
- Program and fund-raising publicity
- Books, newsletters, annual reports, year books
- Statistical and other reports, demographic studies, lecture notes
- Photographs, sound recordings on tape and vinyl
- Videotapes, films and film strips
- Posters, commemorative T-shirts, badges, trophies and other objects
- Artwork, blueprints, maps and other items

CUSTODIAL HISTORY:
- Montreal YMCA donated documents to Concordia University Archives
- First accession moved to Archives on occasion of Downtown YMCA's re-occupation of the renovated Norris Building in 2000 and 2001
- Additional materials received in 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005

CLASSIFICATION PLAN (KEY SERIES):
- P0145/01 — Founding documents, constitution, by-laws, histories
- P0145/02 — Metropolitan Board of Directors
- P0145/04 — Professional Staff
- P0145/05 — Planning, policy, structure
- P0145/11 — Branches, buildings, facilities
- P0145/12 — Camping, outdoor programs
- P0145/14 — External relations

SERIES 12 — CAMPING, OUTDOOR PROGRAMS SUB-SERIES:
- P0145/12A — Committees
- P0145/12B — Kamp Kanawana
- P0145/12C — Camp Otoreke
- P0145/12D — Camp Becsies
- P0145/12E — Camp Dorval
- P0145/12F — Camp Weredale
- P0145/12G — Camp Perrot
- P0145/12H — Ski lodge
- P0145/12I — Camp Thunderbird
- P0145/12J — Wilderness Survival Camp
- P0145/12K — Les Voyageurs de la Vérendrye
- P0145/12L — Lac St-Joseph/Camp Jubilee
- P0145/12M — Day camp
- P0145/12N — Camping associations (ACA, CCA, Quebec Section CCA, QCA/ACQ)

================================================================================
2. KAMP KANAWANA SUB-SERIES (P0145/12B) — MAIN PAGE
   URL: https://concordia.accesstomemory.org/kamp-kanawana
================================================================================

Reference Code: P0145/12B
Dates of Creation: nd, [190-]-2003
Creator: YMCA of Montreal (1851–)

EXTENT:
- 7.72 m of textual records
- Graphic materials (photographs, artwork)
- Objects (t-shirts, badges, ribbons, pennants)
- Cartographic records (maps)
- Architectural and technical drawings
- Sound recordings (audiocassettes)
- Moving images (film reels, videocassettes)
- Other materials

SCOPE AND CONTENT:
- Documents the administration, property, buildings, equipment, publicity, staff, campers, and program of Kamp Kanawana
- Includes directors' reports, annual reports, correspondence, camper applications, blueprints, maps, photographs, publicity brochures and films, t-shirts, badges, ribbons, pennants, and other materials

ARRANGEMENT (SUB-SUB-SERIES):
- P0145/12B01 — General administration
- P0145/12B02 — Financial administration
- P0145/12B03 — Land, facilities, equipment, supplies
- P0145/12B04 — Communications
- P0145/12B05 — Staff, counsellors
- P0145/12B06 — Campers
- P0145/12B07 — Program

RELATED MATERIAL:
- Film: "Kamp Kanawana: The Experience that Lasts a Lifetime"
  - Voiceover narration and camper testimonials
  - Describes camp as "the oldest camp in Quebec and second oldest in Canada"
  - Directed by Cathy Reeves, produced 1993
  - Also exists as colour VHS videocassette, 9 minutes, 1996 version
  - Song "On My Way to Kanawana" composed and performed by Richard Itch Kerr

COMMITTEE AND BOARD RECORDS:
- Special Junior Camp Committee minutes — 1910
- Montreal All-Boys' Camp Committee, Junior Camp Committee minutes, correspondence — 1910-1917
- Kamp Kanawana Committee — 1910-1917
- Kamp Kanawana Committee minutes, Junior Camp Committee minutes, correspondence, financial reports — 1918-1922
- Kamp Kanawana Committee — 1918-1923 (in scrapbook form)
- Kamp Kanawana Committee — 1923-1939 (in scrapbook form)

- Kamp Kanawana Board of Management — 1939
- Kamp Kanawana Board of Management — 1940-1942
- Camp Executive Committee and Board of Management minutes — 1946
- Executive Committee — 1957
- Camp Committee — 1958
- Kamp Kanawana Annual Kommittee Konference — 1961
- Kanawana Committee planning — 1966-1967
- Committee report to Metropolitan Board of Directors — 1967
- Kamp Kanawana Committee meetings — 1968-1969

REPORTS/MINUTES ALSO INCLUDE:
- Reports/minutes of Special Committee in charge of the proposed New Camp for Boys
- Reports/minutes of the Special Junior Camp Committee
- Reports/minutes of the All Montreal Boys' Camp Committee
- Agendas, budgets and financial reports
- Reports of trips and visits to Kamp Kanawana
- Lists of campers
- Correspondence and publicity

MICROFICHES:
- 6 microfiches: "Junior Camp Opening Roster" — 1924-1939
- 3 microfiches: "Permanent Camp Committee" — 1911-1926

OTHER NOTABLE ITEMS:
- Proposed wildlife sanctuary, bird and game sanctuary — 1847, 1954-1960
- Kanawana Reminiscence (of 1948), by Ben T. Hannah — 1989
- YMCA Kamp Kanawana Facts — timeline 1894-1998

NOTES ON ACCESS AND COMPLETENESS
================================================================================

1. The concordia.accesstomemory.org domain was blocked by the egress proxy (403 Forbidden).
   All data extracted via web search engine indexing and cached page content.

2. The concordia.ca finding aid pages were also blocked (403 Forbidden).
   Data extracted via search engine snippets and cached content summaries.

3. The most detailed file-level listings were recovered for:
   - 12B01 (General Administration) — extensive
   - 12B04 (Communications) — extensive
   - 12B07 (Program) — good detail
   - 12B05 (Staff, Counsellors) — partial (research studies identified)
   - 12A (Committees) — extensive

4. Less detail was recovered for:
   - 12B03 (Land, Facilities, Equipment, Supplies) — structure only
   - 12B06 (Campers) — minimal
   - 12B02 (Financial Administration) — structure only

5. A physical visit to the Concordia Archives Special Collections Reading Room
   would yield the complete finding aid and access to the actual materials.

6. The fonds PDF is available at:
   https://concordia.accesstomemory.org/downloads/ymca-of-montreal-fonds-2.pdf
   (blocked by proxy but could be downloaded externally)
